title: multi-tool-exec-docs-parallel-mode-deterministic-injection-retries-and-openai-shim
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Docs refresh for multi-tool execution: updates examples to match current runtime behavior (mode name, header name, event schema), clarifies idempotency requirements for side-effectful tools, and documents default concurrency change (4 -> 8) plus env var override. No product behavior changes introduced by this PR; docs only.
description:
Context: The original runtime PR (redwood#44782) introduced an ergonomic multi-tool execution surface with deterministic tool result injection, per-tool retry policies, streaming markers, and an OpenAI compatibility shim. Since that merge, the runtime implementation and SDK helpers have had a small round of follow-up adjustments (naming and defaults) that left the docs in the monorepo slightly stale for customers reading the docs site. This PR updates the docs site to reflect the current shipped surface while preserving notes about legacy/compat behavior.

What changed in the documented API: 1) Mode naming: docs now describe the primary parallel mode as mode="parallel" (with deterministic injection) and call out that mode="parallel-safe" remains accepted as a legacy alias in 1.14.x for compatibility; 2) Header naming for the OpenAI shim: docs now recommend header "X-Redwood-Tool-Execution: parallel" and note the previous header "X-Redwood-Tool-Exec" as deprecated but still recognized; 3) Streaming event schema: docs now show the normalized SSE/JSON event envelope where the event type field is "type" with values tool_start/tool_delta/tool_end/injection_point (the runtime renamed tool_chunk -> tool_delta); 4) Concurrency defaults: docs now reflect the runtime default orchestrator concurrency of 8 workers (previously 4) and document ORCHESTRATOR_CONCURRENCY as the override, including guidance for private deployments.

Updated examples (docs-only): The request envelope examples remain centered on the top-level tool_execution field and deterministic injection, but the snippet is updated to avoid implying that clients must set inject_results explicitly. Example shown in docs: {"input":"Translate and summarize","tool_execution":{"mode":"parallel","tools":[{"name":"translate","idempotency_key":"tx-123","retry":{"max_attempts":2,"backoff_ms":200},"stream":true},{"name":"summarize","retry":{"max_attempts":1}}]}}. The docs also add a small mapping table for OpenAI-style function_call payloads explaining how tool_call_id maps into Redwood tool identifiers and how ordering is stabilized.

Idempotency and retries clarification: The docs now state that idempotency_key is required only when a tool is declared side-effectful (side_effects=true) and retries are enabled (max_attempts > 1), matching current validator behavior; purely read-only tools may omit idempotency_key even when retries are enabled. The docs also clarify that the server may downgrade parallel execution to sequential when it detects ambiguous side effects or missing idempotency, and that this downgrade is surfaced via a response field in the tool execution summary (documented here; no code changes in this repo).

Migration notes: Added a short section "Upgrading from early-access docs" describing the deprecated mode/header names, and explicitly noting that older clients that send mode="parallel-safe" and/or header "X-Redwood-Tool-Exec" will continue to work during 1.14.x but are planned for removal in a future major release.

Testing/CI: Docs build and link checks pass; updated snippets are validated by the docs-site JSON snippet linter. No runtime code changes included.

Follow-ups: A separate runtime PR will add a dedicated response schema reference page (generated OpenAPI) so the event examples stay in sync automatically; tracked in ENG-6014.
commits: 4 commits: 1) docs/tool-exec: refresh mode/header names + migration notes; 2) docs/streaming: update event schema examples (tool_chunk -> tool_delta); 3) docs/retries: clarify idempotency requirements and downgrade behavior; 4) docs/site: fix anchors, add compatibility table, run snippet linter
review_comments: Priya Kapoor: Please make it explicit which names are deprecated vs current (mode + header) and add a one-line timeline for removal.
Maya Chen (author): Added a "Deprecated" callout box for mode="parallel-safe" and header "X-Redwood-Tool-Exec" and noted "supported throughout 1.14.x; removal no earlier than 1.16".
Alejandro Ruiz: The idempotency rule here contradicts the original PR text (it used to require idempotency_key for any side-effectful tool). Can we confirm current behavior and cite it accurately?

Maya Chen (author): Confirmed in runtime validator: idempotency_key is required when side_effects=true AND retries enabled; updated wording and added an example of server downgrade to sequential when missing.
Nina Patel: The streaming event example should show the exact field names clients should key off of; avoid prose-only descriptions.
Maya Chen (author): Added a concrete JSONL snippet with fields: type, tool_name, tool_call_id, seq, timestamp, and payload.
ci_summary: CI: docs build/pass, link checker/pass, snippet linter/pass, spellcheck/pass.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash after approvals. Docs-only change; no backport required.
notes_for_backport: None (docs site deploy picks up main). If syncing docs into private bundles, include in next docs bundle cut.
ui_changes: Docs site: updated tool execution quickstart, added migration page for early-access naming, and updated streaming events reference with new tool_delta examples.
observability: N/A (docs-only). Documented current metrics names as: tool_exec.invocations, tool_exec.retry_count, tool_exec.concurrent_workers, tool_exec.injection_latency_ms.
incident_tieins: Documents the deterministic injection and downgrade-to-sequential behavior that was introduced after INC-2026 learnings; no incident remediation code in this repo.
